name: Assi Ghat
description: Southernmost ghat popular with travelers and students. Morning yoga, chai stalls, and subah-e-banaras program.

name: BHU & New Vishwanath Temple
description: Banaras Hindu University campus with the modern Vishwanath Temple — largest temple complex in North India.

name: Blue Lassi Shop
description: Legendary tiny shop serving thick fruit lassi since 1925.

name: Chunar Fort
description: Ancient fort 40 km from Varanasi on the Ganges. Used by Mughal and British rulers. Legends of supernatural events.

name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
description: Main ghat where the spectacular Ganga Aarti happens every evening at sunset.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
description: One of 12 Jyotirlingas — the most sacred Shiva temple in India.

name: Manikarnika Ghat
description: Primary cremation ghat burning 24/7 for thousands of years. Most sacred site for Hindu cremation rites.

name: Panchganga Ghat
description: Sacred ghat where five rivers are said to meet. Alamgir Mosque (former Bindu Madhava temple) towers above.

name: Ramnagar Fort
description: Fort-palace of the Maharaja of Varanasi across the Ganges. Museum with vintage cars, ivory, and weapons.

name: Sarnath
description: Where Buddha gave his first sermon. Dhamek Stupa and archaeological museum.

name: Tulsi Manas Temple
description: Modern marble temple where Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas. Walls inscribed with the entire epic text.

name: Gulmarg Golf Course
description: World's highest green golf course at 8,700 ft. 18 holes surrounded by snow-capped peaks.

name: Gulmarg Gondola
description: World's second-highest operating cable car reaching 14,000 ft. Two phases with views of Nanga Parbat and K2.

name: Khilanmarg
description: Alpine meadow above Gulmarg with direct views of Nanga Parbat and Harmukh peak. Wildflowers in summer.

name: Maharani Temple (Rani Temple)
description: Hilltop Shiva temple built by Maharaja Hari Singh's wife. Stunning views of Gulmarg meadow.

name: Strawberry Valley
description: Lush meadow known for wild strawberries in summer. Horse riding with Himalayan backdrop.

name: Kaza Main Bazaar
description: The 300-metre main street that carries every cafe, gear shop, money-changer, and SIM vendor in Spiti. Last reliable ATM before Tabo/Komic is here (SBI).

name: Key Monastery Viewpoint
description: 7km from Kaza on the Kibber road — the classic photo stop for Key Gompa stacked up the hillside. 11th-century founding, largest monastery in Spiti.

name: Sakya Tangyud Monastery
description: The original seat of the Sakya sect in Spiti, 2km above Kaza town. The walled fortress-style complex houses 30+ monks and a decorated dukhang (prayer hall).

name: Spiti River Ghat
description: 5-minute walk below the main market. Cold river running through the valley floor — locals do their prayers and offerings here at sunset.

name: Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra
description: Indo-Islamic mosque built in 1199, originally a Sanskrit college. Seven arches with intricate calligraphy.

name: Ajmer Sharif Dargah
description: Sufi shrine of Moinuddin Chishti (1236). One of the most important Muslim pilgrimages in India. Visited by all faiths.

name: Ana Sagar Lake
description: Artificial lake created in 1135. Mughal-era marble pavilions (Baradari) on the promenade. Sunset spot.

name: Chandrashila Peak
description: Summit at 13,000 ft above Tungnath with 360-degree Himalayan panorama including Nanda Devi and Chaukhamba.

name: Deoria Tal
description: Emerald lake at 7,841 ft reflecting Chaukhamba peaks. Popular camping and trekking destination from Sari village.

name: Tungnath Trek from Chopta
description: World's highest Shiva temple at 12,073 ft. 3.5 km trek through rhododendron forests from Chopta.

name: Brahma Sarovar
description: One of India's largest sacred tanks. Site where Lord Brahma performed a yajna to create the universe.

name: Jyotisar (Bhagavad Gita Birthplace)
description: Sacred spot where Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna. Banyan tree marks the chariot site.

name: Kurukshetra Panorama & Science Centre
description: Cylindrical building with 360-degree painting of the Mahabharata war. Interactive science exhibits.

name: Erumeli Petta Thullal
description: Starting point for the traditional 60km route to Sabarimala. Pilgrims gather here for the longer, austere Mala-clad (celibate) pilgrimage. Less common than Pamba but spiritually significant.

name: Pamba Ghats
description: Sacred bathing point where pilgrims purify before the trek. Confluence of Pamba, Achankovil, and Manimala rivers. Simple guest houses and the start of the trekking trail.

name: Sannidhanam Temple Complex
description: The main Ayyappa shrine at 914m peak. The sanctum sanctorum houses the deity's idol. The vast open courtyard can hold thousands of pilgrims during season.

name: Bangus Forest Trail
description: Dense deodar and pine forest walk with wildlife sightings. Bears, leopards, and musk deer habitat.

name: Bangus Valley Meadow
description: Pristine alpine meadow surrounded by snow-capped peaks. One of Kashmir's most untouched valleys.

name: Girnar Ropeway
description: Cable car to the first peak (Ambaji temple at 2,700 ft). Panoramic views of Junagadh and Saurashtra plains.

name: Neminath Jain Temple
description: 2,500-year-old Jain temple at the summit. Exquisite marble carvings. Reward after the gruelling climb.

name: Kumbhalgarh Fort
description: UNESCO World Heritage fort with world's second-longest continuous wall (36 km). Birth place of Maharana Pratap.

name: Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Sanctuary in the Aravalli Hills connecting Kumbhalgarh to Ranakpur. Wolves, leopards, and sloth bears.

name: Char Dham
description: Replica of India's four Char Dham temples at one location with a 108-ft Shiva statue. Pilgrimage theme park.

name: Samdruptse Statue
description: 135-ft copper statue of Guru Padmasambhava on a hilltop. Second-largest statue in Sikkim.

name: Jal Mandir (Water Temple)
description: Small shrine halfway through the parikrama dedicated to water. Pilgrims believe drinking water here grants blessings. Natural spring feeds the temple.

name: Parasnath Hill Temples
description: Supreme Jain pilgrimage site with 24 temples on Parasnath Hill. Highest peak in Jharkhand at 4,480 ft.

name: Alchi Monastery
description: Rare 11th-century Kashmiri-style Buddhist monastery with Indo-European art. Wooden carvings and murals.

name: Dholavira UNESCO Site
description: UNESCO Harappan city with advanced water management, citadel, ceremonial ground, and the famous Indus script signboard.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove preserved for centuries by the Khasi people. No leaf or twig may be removed.

name: Rudraprayag Sangam
description: Sacred confluence of Alaknanda and Mandakini rivers. Important stop on the Char Dham yatra route.
